 Corona trial videos brought up by Duterte impeachment defense
 Jaehwa Bernardo ,
 Allison Co ,
 Katrina Domingo ,
 ABS-CBN News
 Published November 19, 2026 12:54 PM PHT 
  | 
 Updated November 19, 2026 02:59 PM PHT 
 Anti-money laundering and financial crime lawyer Rainer dela Fuente takes the witness stand for the defense on the 44th day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial at the Senate in Pasay City on Thursday, November 19, 2026. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News  MANILA (UPDATED) — Vice President Sara Duterte's defense team presented Thursday videos from the previous impeachment trial of the late Chief Justice Renato Corona, prompting senator-judges to question their relevance to the current proceedings and a prosecutor to accuse the panel of trying to appeal to emotion.
 When Duterte's impeachment trial  resumed following a brief break to make way for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit hosted by the Philippines, the defense presented anti-money laundering compliance practitioner Rainer dela Fuente as an expert witness.
 Dela Fuente, who is a certified public accountant and lawyer, was called to counter claims made by the prosecution about the bank transactions of the Vice President and her husband during a previous testimony by an Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) official.
 During direct examination, the defense, led by lawyer Mark Vinluan, played a video of the late Sen. Miriam Defensor Santiago during Corona's impeachment trial in late 2011 to 2012. In the footage, Santiago berated the prosecution for withdrawing five of the eight articles of impeachment against Corona, who was eventually removed from office.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 The prosecution in Duterte's case made a similar move, withdrawing three of the four impeachment charges against the Vice President. Duterte now faces the sole charge of allegedly amassing unexplained wealth.
 After the video was played, however, Sens. Erwin Tulfo and Panfilo "Ping" Lacson questioned its relevance to the ongoing proceedings.
 Tulfo said it was "like watching a movie" and said the dead should be left in peace.
 "That is a different case, this is a different case. This is a different set of senators... I really do not understand why we're watching this," he said, with presiding officer Sen. Francis "Chiz" Escudero agreeing.
 Lacson said he could not see why the "opinion [of] one of the 24 senator-judges in the 2011 impeach trial of the late [Chief] Justice Corona" is significant to the Duterte case.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Later, the defense played another video from Corona’s impeachment trial, showing the late chief justice becoming emotional as he defended himself and described the "chilling effect" of the proceedings on the Supreme Court and his personal life.
 Sen. Raffy Tulfo noted that Corona was ultimately convicted for his failure to fully disclose his assets and bank deposits. 
 After playing the videos, including one showing former President Rodrigo Duterte being asked about the possibility of impeaching then Vice President Leni Robredo, Vinluan asked Dela Fuente how information from the AMLC could be used as a "political weapon" in an impeachment trial.
 "It can, the possibility is still there," Dela Fuente said.
 Responding to questions from Vinluan, Dela Fuente also cited a provision of the Anti-Money Laundering Act that prohibits the use of information obtained by the AMLC for political persecution.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 LIVE UPDATES: Vice President Sara Duterte's Impeachment Trial (Day 44)
 'APPEAL TO EMOTION' House prosecutor Chel Diokno of Akbayan Party-List said he did not see the relevance of Corona's statements in the videos played, adding that it was only an "appeal to emotion" that he said has no place in the impeachment trial. 
 "Whatever question is asked [related to the video], it would be immaterial, it would be irrelevant, it would constitute hearsay because we cannot even cross-examine the late Chief Justice Corona on his statements. And it would be misleading because there is no such evidence of persecution in this case before the court," Diokno added.
 Sen. Risa Hontiveros also said it was "not fair" to bring up Santiago, Corona and former President Rodrigo Duterte during the trial, as none of the senator-judges could ask them about their statements.
 Vinluan also asked Dela Fuente about the confidentiality of AMLC reports and the bank records of the vice president and her husband, which had earlier been presented before the impeachment court.
 READ: AMLC received reports on P4.4-B transactions involving Sara Duterte, husband The prosecution had also given such financial records to financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera, which was used to produce the report that concluded Duterte's undeclared wealth supposedly accumulated to P817.87 million from 2022 to 2025. 
 ADVERTISEMENT
 READ: Suspicious transaction reports not conclusions of illegal activity, says AMLC official
 However, Sens. Raffy Tulfo and Francis Pangilinan said the issue of confidentiality had been settled, noting that the impeachment court is exempt from laws governing the confidentiality of such records.
 'BAD TASTE'   In a press briefing during the trial's lunch break, the prosecution described the presentation of videos showing Santiago and Corona as being in "bad taste" and "unethical."
 "Now that they have presented mga namayapang tao, I think this also speaks about patay na po ang kaso ng depensa," House prosecution spokesperson Zia Alonto Adiong of Lanao del Sur's 1st District said.
 (Now that they have presented deceased people, I think this also speaks about how their case is dead.)
 For Manila 3rd District Rep. Joel Chua, another House prosecutor, the defense wasted the court's time by presenting the videos, which he also viewed as an appeal to the public's emotions.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Counsel for prosecutors Amando Virgil Ligutan accused the defense of “exploiting the dead.” 
 “They are supposed to present mga buhay na witnesses… Binubuhay nila yung mga namayapa na,” he told reporters.
 “Siguro wala na pong buhay na tao na gusto mag-defend sa Vice President that’s why they are going for something unusual, bringing back the dead. Nakakahiya naman po sa mga namayapang officials,” he said.
 ‘MIND CONDITIONING’  
 But Duterte's spokesman, lawyer Paolo Panelo, defended her counsel and said these videos were just preliminary to the defense's turn to present its own set of evidence. 
 “Antayin po nila kasi alam naman po nila na may pagkakataon yung defense na mag-present ng ebidensya,” he said. 
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Panelo also called out the prosecution for “mind-conditioning” the public over their statements to the media. 
 “Huwag po nilang i-mind condition yung mga tao doon sa mga opinion nila… doon sila magaling eh. Yung magpaparatang sila pero hindi bibigyan ng karapatan or oportunidad yung depensa na makasagot,” Panelo added.
